summary: The ffmpeg `-t` duration cap silently truncates over-limit audio, so the `len(pcm) > max_pcm_bytes` refusal can never fire and a clipped SpeechChunk is delivered as complete.
failure_scenario: Synthesized MP3 decodes to more PCM than max_pcm_bytes (e.g. long 4096-char segment, or a 16 MiB default cap at 48 kHz mono, about 175 s) -> ffmpeg stops at exactly max_pcm_bytes with exit 0 -> _build_chunk accepts it (not > cap) -> the SpeechChunk carries the full `text` but audio missing its tail, so the user hears a cut-off reply that is reported as fully spoken.
evidence: Decoded a 3 s sine MP3 through EdgeTtsSynthesizer(sample_rate_hz=16000, max_pcm_bytes=64000) with a stub synthesize_mp3: the chunk returned 64000 bytes (2 s) with the full text and no exception. The `> max_pcm_bytes` check in _ffmpeg_decode and _build_chunk is unreachable for decoder overflow. tests/providers/test_edge_tts.py has no truncation test (grep for -t/truncat finds none).

summary: vad.py WebRtcVoiceActivityDetector: exact-type validation, frame-size/format checks, start/end debounce and reset are consistent; no defect found.

speech_presence.py: AudioFrame guarantees non-empty even-length PCM so max() on empty probabilities and frombuffer odd-length cannot occur; custom model_path skipping the SHA pin is a documented-looking design choice, not asserted as a defect.
edge_tts.py cancel/close/duplicate-turn bookkeeping: operation map is cleaned in finally paths and ffmpeg process is killed on BaseException; no leak found in the time box.

scripts/full_purge_worker.py: Windows-only isolated worker with nonce/ack framing and handle closing in finally; no defect found.
